Stated Claim / Post Context:
Racist woman nicknamed 'Proposal Karen' shrieks 'Go back to Mexico' as Hispanic man asks girlfriend to marry him at California beauty spot

The engagement of Emmanuel Banuelos and his now-fiancée Hayley Lugos set in a Laguna Beach park was disturbed by a woman, nicknamed Proposal Karen.

Actual Article Body:
By VICTOR HELLER, US REPORTER

Published:  02:27 AEST, 7 October 2026   |  Updated:  04:19 AEST, 7 October 2026

A California woman was caught interrupting a picture-perfect proposal at a coastline beauty spot with a racist rant last week.

The engagement of Emmanuel Banuelos and his now-fiancée Hayley Lugos set in a Laguna Beach park was disturbed by a woman, who was given the nickname Proposal Karen after the clip of her interruption went viral online.

While two crew members were filming and photographing the setting minutes before the romantic moment, an irate Orange County woman can be seen passing by with her dog.

Suddenly, the woman can be seen approaching the two and saying: 'The park is for people that live here to enjoy the park and have picnics.

'And they don't allow events on the grass here for that reason.'

A female crew member, later identified as the newly engaged fiancée's sister, responded: 'Yeah, I understand, ma'am.'

However, the grumpy dog owner snaps at her: 'I just called the police. They're coming out here. They're going to make you tear it down.'

The crew member tried calming down the woman and assuring her they would be gone right after the proposal but only received a disgruntled response: 'I don't care. It's every single f*****g weekend and I'm sick and tired of it.'

What was meant to be a romantic moment for Emmanuel Banuelos and Hayley Lugos, was interrupted by a disgruntled dog owner nicknamed Proposal Karen

The furious Laguna Beach resident attacked the video crew waiting to capture the picture-perfect proposal

After repeatedly asking them to tear down the engagement setup, the woman escalated and shouted: 'Go back to Mexico'

Despite more efforts to calm down the Proposal Karen, the conflict intensified as she kept demanding that everyone involved in the proposal tear down the setup and leave the park, before the couple could get engaged.

The woman's aggression peaked when a mariachi band started playing Hispanic music: 'Bullsh*t! F*****g Mexican. This isn't Mexico either, you motherf*****s.'

She storms off shouting at the video crew: 'Go back to Mexico!'

Banuelos described the Proposal Karen as a 'miserable person' attempting to destroy a romantic moment, to KTLA.

Speaking to the LA Times, Lugos said: 'It made me feel so sad that people still have so much hate and racism in them. When I saw it and heard it, my heart sank. It just left me distraught.'

A video of the incident reached more than 11 million views and one million likes on Instagram. 'Mind you, engagements are not prohibited at this park and this proposal lasted less than 40 minutes,' the account named Trinity Films wrote in its caption.

Users are supportive of the Latino couple with some shocked about the woman's racist remarks and others highlighting Southern California's ties to Mexico.

A spokesperson for the city of Laguna Beach told the LA Times the city was aware of the video and that it does not support hateful language and behavior.

Despite the woman's racist remarks, the newly-engaged couple celebrated the romantic milestone and returned home to Ontario

'Laguna Beach's parks and beaches are open to everyone and are regularly the backdrop to celebrate milestones,' the spokesperson said in a statement.

'Because of their frequency, they can also affect the general public's right to enjoy the coastline. Therefore, pre-planned setups and professional photography have specific rules and permit requirements.'

The spokesperson did not reveal whether this specific proposal violated any rules but added that documented proposals require a professional photography approval and that proposals with set-ups and structures are not allowed.

Banuelos told the LA Times he did not think he needed a professional photography permit because the videographer was a family member.

The couple said they returned home to Ontario, where they celebrated their engagement despite the hateful interruption.
